---
title: "League tables and report cards"
subtitle: "1.1 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024): their firms and their report cards"
description: "Comparison of pairwise statements in a strict ranking and KRW's report cards for 97 firms."
---

Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), hereafter KRW, estimated race and gender contact gaps from fictitious applications
sent to 97 large U.S. employers. The gaps measure contact advantages for distinctively white over Black names and
male over female names. Ranking the estimates states a direction for every firm pair. KRW's cards state directions
between grades only, and these can disagree with the estimate ranking. The displays compare the statements for
each firm.

```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Race card.** The table states a direction for each of the 4,656 pairs of firms. KRW's race card states 1,324 of
  them (.284): 1,219 run as the table does and 105 the other way; it is silent on the other 3,332.
- **Second place.** Nationwide is second by estimate (.402 ± .216) but shares grade 2 with 80 other firms. Of its pairs
  with the other 96 firms, the card states 16: 15 as the table does and 1 the other way, Genuine Parts (sixth by
  estimate) above it.
- **Last place.** State Farm has the lowest race estimate, −.544, and the largest SE, .444, yet stands at rank 14 by
  posterior mean (.155), pulled up by KRW's race prior ([normal–normal posterior shrinkage](shrinkage.qmd)). Of its 16 stated
  pairs: 2 as the table does and 14 the other way.
- **By posterior mean.** Genuine Parts (Napa Auto) now leads (.250), though sixth by estimate (.330 ± .071). It shares
  grade 1 with AutoNation, the largest estimate (.433). Now every one of the card's 1,324 directions runs as the table
  does.
- **Gender card.** The table now ranks the gender estimates. The card's four grades, sizes 1, 3, 89, 4, state 731 pairs
  (.157): 730 run as the table does and 1 the other way. Builders FirstSource is alone in grade 1, so all 96 of its
  pairs are stated.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Sources: KRW's Introduction and Section VI, "Racial Discrimination Report Cards" (Figure 7, the race card), Section
VIII (Figure 14, the gender card), and talk slides 4–5 and 61–63 (card layout after slides 61–63). On the race card,
grade 1 is KRW's ★ (one star), which KRW call the worst grade. A shared grade means "not compared", not "equal". Data:
Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), doi:10.1257/aer.20230700, and deposit doi:10.3886/E198284V1; CC-BY-NC as stated by the
deposit (no version), noncommercial use only; as adapted in postrank 1.1.0 (pr_case_krw), changes noted; no
endorsement by the authors is implied. The data describe KRW's correspondence experiment, not any firm's current
conduct.
:::

library(postrank)
pr_case_krw$reference$single_criterion$archive_metrics[, c("criterion", "grade_sizes", "N", "M", "s")]  # race 2/81/14: 1324 of 4656; gender 1/3/89/4: 731
head(pr_case_krw$units[order(-pr_case_krw$units$race_estimate), c("firm_name", "race_estimate", "race_se")], 2)  # AutoNation 0.4332195, Nationwide 0.4022631
```
